gen_risks.description: Delay to Final Investment Decision and Commercial Operation Date could push the project timeline.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate a 6‑month schedule buffer, align procurement with spurline timeline, and monitor critical path milestones weekly.
gen_risks.evidence: Option 2: Padeswood Delayed ... resulting in a subsequent 5‑month delay to COD.

gen_risks.description: First‑of‑a‑kind CCS technology may not meet performance targets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a pilot capture unit, conduct performance testing against thresholds, and retain WSP technical oversight throughout construction.
gen_risks.evidence: first‑of‑a‑kind CCS deployment; independent technical assurance by WSP confirmed viability.

gen_risks.description: Revenue under the ICC Contract could be delayed or reduced, affecting cash flow.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include escrow or bank guarantee for ICC payments, and define clear payment triggers linked to verified capture volumes.
gen_risks.evidence: ICC Contract provides revenue support per tonne of CO₂ captured, offering long‑term certainty over income.

gen_risks.description: Project could be discontinued before completion, leading to sunk costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure multi‑year funding commitments via legally binding grant agreements and stage‑gate reviews before major expenditures.
gen_risks.evidence: Discontinuation risk for Padeswood listed under Financial Risks.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient grant funding (CIF) may cause capital cost overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain a contingency reserve of at least 10% of capital cost and explore alternative financing if grant shortfall occurs.
gen_risks.evidence: CIF Grant provides upfront capital support ... up to 50% of eligible capital costs.

gen_risks.description: Cross‑chain integration risks could delay CO₂ transport and storage connections.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated cross‑chain coordination team, formal interface agreements, and regular integration workshops between Padeswood and T&S network owners.
gen_risks.evidence: Managing government‑owned cross‑chain delivery risks and operating model integration risks.

gen_risks.description: Changes to CCS Network Code or related legislation may affect compliance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Embed change‑in‑law and regulatory review clauses in contracts, and maintain ongoing liaison with Ofgem and the CCS Network Code authority.
gen_risks.evidence: Padeswood is compliant with the CCS Network Code and contracts include change‑in‑law clauses.

gen_risks.description: Carbon price volatility and CBAM implementation could reduce competitiveness of UK cement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Lock in long‑term revenue through the ICC Contract, model scenarios for carbon price and CBAM tariffs, and retain operational flexibility.
gen_risks.evidence: UK cement sector is at risk of carbon leakage. The UK Carbon‑Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) will be introduced in 2027.

gen_risks.description: Potential fraud or misuse of grant funds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strict grant administration controls, independent audits, and real‑time monitoring of expenditures by DESNZ CGL.

gen_risks.description: Cost inflation for capital and operating expenses may erode project economics.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply escalation clauses tied to CPI and energy price indices, and allocate a cost‑inflation contingency of 5‑7% of total budget.
gen_risks.evidence: Open Book Model ... integrating inflation and energy assumptions.

gen_risks.description: Governance weaknesses could lead to poor decision‑making and overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define clear governance structures, assign responsibility matrices, and conduct quarterly oversight meetings with all governing bodies.
gen_risks.evidence: Governance and Oversight ... Ofgem, LCCC, DESNZ CGL, Cluster Function Team.

gen_risks.description: Force majeure events (e.g., pandemics) may disrupt construction or operation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Negotiate comprehensive force‑majeure provisions and obtain appropriate insurance coverage for major disruption events.

gen_risks.description: Project maturity uncertainties could cause technical or schedule setbacks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Progress through defined maturity milestones, with independent technical reviews at each stage before proceeding to the next.
gen_risks.evidence: Project Maturity and Development Status heading indicates maturity considerations.

gen_risks.description: Dependence on the HyNet T&S network capacity; network delays would impact capture utilisation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Synchronise Padeswood construction schedule with T&S network delivery, and develop fallback transport options if network delays occur.
gen_risks.evidence: Padeswood will increase the T&S network utilisation and cross‑chain delivery risks are noted.

gen_risks.description: Policy shift or loss of government support could withdraw subsidies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Embed support in legislation (Energy Act 2023) and secure multi‑year policy commitments through formal agreements with the Secretary of State.
gen_risks.evidence: Government intervention is necessary ... future market phases expected to operate with reduced subsidy support.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate data‑management may hinder monitoring and evaluation of benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a data‑management plan, assign data stewards, and implement secure data‑sharing platforms reviewed quarterly.
gen_risks.evidence: Developing a data management strategy, including reviewing relevant data sharing arrangements.

gen_risks.description: Shortage of skilled workforce for CCS operation could delay commissioning.
gen_risks.mitigation: Partner with training providers, develop apprenticeship schemes, and allocate budget for upskilling of CCS operational staff.
gen_risks.evidence: Stimulate the CCUS supply chain, jobs, and skills over the support contracts’ lifespans.

gen_risks.description: Financial model sensitivities to key assumptions may affect projected viability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Perform robust sensitivity analysis on key financial assumptions and update the business case annually.
gen_risks.evidence: Financial sensitivities listed under Financial Risks.

gt_risks.description: Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) risk. RSA would be paid to the T&S Company (Eni) in two circumstances: where the network is underutilised, and where users are unavailable to inject CO2 and therefore are not paying user fees. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.1, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Padeswood joining the T&S network will reduce the level of network underutilisation and will therefore reduce RSA payments to the T&SCo.

gt_risks.description: Discontinuation risk for Padeswood: the potential for Padeswood to be unable to continue under the business model contract due to the actions of another party or events outside its control - a large-scale, programme-wide issue (e.g. leakage), a prolonged T&S issue, or external events such as Qualifying Change in Law (QCiL), Qualifying Shutdown Events, or Force Majeure. Projects connected via a spurline can also be exposed to an additional risk if the spurline FID is taken after T&S FID, which is not within the capture project's control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.2, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: The risk of having to make a discontinuation payment to Padeswood is judged to be a remote contingent liability given that it is very unlikely (<1%); spurline-timing risk is treated as a variation of the existing cross-chain risks already protected by the business model.

gt_risks.description: Exchequer funding / Secretary of State direct agreement (SoSDA) risk: LCCC is only liable to make payments to the extent it has received sufficient funds from HMG, creating a risk that Padeswood would have no recourse under its private-law contract with LCCC to obtain payments owed if HMG funding to LCCC were insufficient. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.3, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: The Secretary of State will sign a direct agreement with Padeswood (to which LCCC is also party) to fund payments directly where LCCC fails to pay; this does not increase DESNZ's overall liabilities or create a contingent liability, as it is an intragroup transaction.

gt_risks.description: Fraud risk across the CCUS programme's grant and contract payments. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.4, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: A CCUS Fraud Management Strategy is being developed specifying the programme's strategic approach to deterrence, prevention, detection, and management of fraud and error, including counter-fraud governance and reporting structures and high-quality fraud risk assessments (FRAs) for the different tranches of the CCUS programme.

gt_risks.description: Financial sensitivities: several contractual terms are 'locked in' at Padeswood FID, but drivers of the financial impact continue to move post-FID - notably the carbon market price (Low ETS series used as the reference price for the extension period) and the opex reopener (higher opex expenditure payments), both of which could result in higher subsidy. Other financial sensitivities have the effect of reducing total subsidy. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.5, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Sensitivity analysis has been conducted to estimate the scale of potential subsidy increase from each driver; offsetting sensitivities are also identified and tracked.

gt_risks.description: Cross-chain and cross-cutting risks. Cross-chain risks are risks the private sector is exposed to through the network but cannot mitigate against - T&S Construction delay, Padeswood Construction Delay, Padeswood Underperformance, T&S Underperformance, and Discontinuation Provisions; Padeswood joining the HyNet cluster increases HMG's exposure to compensation payments should the T&S network fail or become unavailable. Cross-cutting risks - inflation risk, carbon price risk, and OpEx risk - are those which are challenging for the private sector to price or relate to events outside their control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.6, p.14-15; overlaps in subject matter with the Economic Case's Sec 3.4 Risk Appraisal tables, p.10-11, which quantify the value-for-money impact of the same named risks but are a modelling input rather than a risk-register entry, and are excised from planning text for leakage safety but not scored here.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Risk allocation is designed so that each risk sits with the party best placed to manage it; the business model contracts and Network Code are structured to limit and price cross-chain exposure.
